title: The framework for judicial review under the APA
shortTitle: The framework for judicial review under the APA
summary: Judicial review separates access to court, the action being challenged, the standard of review, and the available remedy.
notes:
The APA supplies an authorization and framework for review; a separate statute supplies subject-matter jurisdiction. Section 702 addresses who may challenge agency action, § 703 the form and venue, § 704 the actions reviewable, and § 706 the reviewing court’s task. Injunctions and declarations are conventional remedies. Agency-specific statutes can create review routes with their own form, timing, and conditions.

Scope of review concerns the intensity and kind of examination. Legal interpretation, factfinding, discretionary policy, and procedural compliance present different questions, even when joined in one case. The introduction explains the institutional tension between enforcing legal limits and preserving the responsibilities assigned to administrators and elected institutions. The assigned questions ask who should be able to enforce public duties and how legal, political, technical, and equitable concerns affect the timing and intensity of review.
